+# dip — 《DiP: Taming Diffusion Models in Pixel Space》学习区
+
+**论文**：DiP: Taming Diffusion Models in Pixel Space  
+**arXiv**：[2511.18822v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18822v3)，25 页（正文 1–8，参考文献 9–11，附录 12–25，76 条文献）  
+**作者**：Zhennan Chen, Junwei Zhu, Xu Chen, Jiangning Zhang, Xiaobin Hu, Hanzhen Zhao, Chengjie Wang, Jian Yang, Ying Tai  
+**代码**：[`../../DiP/`](../../DiP/)（官方仓库 [NJU-PCALab/DiP](https://github.com/NJU-PCALab/DiP)）
+
+## 这是什么
+
+DiP 是一个不依赖 VAE 的像素空间扩散框架。它把生成拆成两部分：DiT backbone
+在大 patch 上建立全局结构，轻量 Patch Detailer Head（PDH）利用局部归纳偏置恢复细节。
+论文报告 PDH 仅增加约 0.3% 参数，在 ImageNet 256×256 上达到 FID 1.79；速度主张和
+比较口径应回到正文 Table 1（PDF p5）核对。
+
+## 阅读入口
+
+- [`paper/2511.18822v3_dip.pdf`](paper/2511.18822v3_dip.pdf)：arXiv v3 原文。
+- [`paper/paper_by_page.txt`](paper/paper_by_page.txt)：逐页文本，页码引用以这里的标记为准。
+- [`paper/paper_layout.txt`](paper/paper_layout.txt)：保留双栏布局，读取 Table 1–4 时使用。
+- [`paper/paper_raw.txt`](paper/paper_raw.txt)：全文关键词检索。
+- [`paper/references.md`](paper/references.md)：76 条参考文献，编号完整、无缺号或重号。
+- [`paper/figures/`](paper/figures/)：正文全部图表页，以及附录的超参数与 PDH 分析页。
+
+## 论文结构与页码
+
+| 章节 | PDF 页 | 内容 |
+|---|---:|---|
+| Abstract + §1 | 1–2 | 问题设定、与 latent/pixel diffusion 的成本比较 |
+| §2–§3 | 2–5 | 相关工作、动机、DiT + Patch Detailer Head |
+| §4–§5 | 5–8 | 主结果、分析、消融与结论 |
+| References | 9–11 | 76 条文献 |
+| Supplementary | 12–25 | 理论分析、训练细节、更多 PDH 实验与样本 |
+
+## 溯源
+
+由 [`../new_paper.sh`](../new_paper.sh) 收入：
+
+```bash
+./new_paper.sh dip 2511.18822v3 "1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 18 19" 9:11
+```
+
+PDF SHA-256：`0a855dcd2383d36b98eb02e0fc494734da01b183bdef470bedc4bc6881684f26`。

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Direct, single-node launcher for GRACE on 4 x A100 40 GB GPUs.
+#
+# Required environment variables:
+#   MODEL_NAME_OR_PATH  local Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct directory
+#   TEACHER_MODEL_PATH  local Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct directory
+#   SHAREGPT4V_ROOT     ShareGPT4V directory described in the root README
+#
+# Typical invocation:
+#   MODEL_NAME_OR_PATH=/models/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct \
+#   TEACHER_MODEL_PATH=/models/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct \
+#   SHAREGPT4V_ROOT=/datasets/ShareGPT4V \
+#   OUTPUT_DIR=/checkpoints/qwen3vl-2b-grace-w4g128 \
+#   bash scripts/finetune_qwen3vl_2b_grace_4gpu.sh
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+PROJECT_DIR=${PROJECT_DIR:-"$(dirname -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}")"}
+
+: "${MODEL_NAME_OR_PATH:?Set MODEL_NAME_OR_PATH to the local Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct directory}"
+: "${TEACHER_MODEL_PATH:?Set TEACHER_MODEL_PATH to the local Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct directory}"
+: "${SHAREGPT4V_ROOT:?Set SHAREGPT4V_ROOT to the ShareGPT4V dataset root}"
+
+BASE_MODEL_DIR=${MODEL_NAME_OR_PATH}
+DATASETS=${DATASETS:-sharegpt4v_mix665k}
+
+QAT_BITS=${QAT_BITS:-4}
+QAT_GROUP_SIZE=${QAT_GROUP_SIZE:-128}
+QAT_SCALE_LR=${QAT_SCALE_LR:-2e-4}
+
+DKD_TEMPERATURE=${DKD_TEMPERATURE:-2.0}
+DKD_ALPHA=${DKD_ALPHA:-1.0}
+DKD_BETA=${DKD_BETA:-4.0}
+RCKA_WEIGHT=${RCKA_WEIGHT:-3.0}
+RCKA_LAYER=${RCKA_LAYER:--2}
+IB_TAU=${IB_TAU:-3.0}
+IB_ETA=${IB_ETA:-0.003}
+IB_BETA_INIT=${IB_BETA_INIT:-0.5}
+IB_BETA_MIN=${IB_BETA_MIN:-0.1}
+IB_BETA_MAX=${IB_BETA_MAX:-1.0}
+DKD_WARMUP_STEPS=${DKD_WARMUP_STEPS:-0}
+RCKA_WARMUP_STEPS=${RCKA_WARMUP_STEPS:-400}
+
+LEARNING_RATE=${LEARNING_RATE:-1e-5}
+WEIGHT_DECAY=${WEIGHT_DECAY:-1e-3}
+WARMUP_RATIO=${WARMUP_RATIO:-0.03}
+MAX_GRAD_NORM=${MAX_GRAD_NORM:-1.0}
+# The upstream launcher defaults to one epoch, but its own comment says the
+# reported paper run uses three. Use one here only for a pipeline smoke test.
+NUM_TRAIN_EPOCHS=${NUM_TRAIN_EPOCHS:-3}
+
+# Reference GRACE: 16 GPUs x micro-batch 2 x accumulation 16 = 512.
+# This launcher:     4 GPUs x micro-batch 1 x accumulation 128 = 512.
+NPROC_PER_NODE=${NPROC_PER_NODE:-4}
+PER_DEVICE_BATCH=${PER_DEVICE_BATCH:-1}
+GRAD_ACCUM=${GRAD_ACCUM:-128}
+
+MODEL_MAX_LENGTH=${MODEL_MAX_LENGTH:-8192}
+MAX_PIXELS=${MAX_PIXELS:-200704}
+MIN_PIXELS=${MIN_PIXELS:-784}
+SAVE_STEPS=${SAVE_STEPS:-500}
+SAVE_TOTAL_LIMIT=${SAVE_TOTAL_LIMIT:-3}
+
+RUN_NAME=${RUN_NAME:-"qwen3vl-2b-grace-w${QAT_BITS}g${QAT_GROUP_SIZE}-4gpu"}
+OUTPUT_DIR=${OUTPUT_DIR:-"${PROJECT_DIR}/checkpoints/${RUN_NAME}"}
+DEEPSPEED_CONFIG=${DEEPSPEED_CONFIG:-"${PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/zero2.json"}
+
+export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-0,1,2,3}
+export HF_HOME=${HF_HOME:-"${PROJECT_DIR}/.cache/huggingface"}
+export HF_DATASETS_CACHE=${HF_DATASETS_CACHE:-"${HF_HOME}/datasets"}
+export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=${HF_HUB_OFFLINE:-1}
+export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=${TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE:-1}
+export HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=${HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE:-1}
+export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
+export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-"${OUTPUT_DIR}/wandb"}
+export OMP_NUM_THREADS=${OMP_NUM_THREADS:-8}
+
+export TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
+export TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT=1
+export TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC=900
+export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=${PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF:-expandable_segments:True}
+
+for executable in python torchrun; do
+    if ! command -v "${executable}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        echo "ERROR: ${executable} is not available; activate the GRACE training environment." >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+done
+
+for path in "${BASE_MODEL_DIR}" "${TEACHER_MODEL_PATH}" "${SHAREGPT4V_ROOT}" "${DEEPSPEED_CONFIG}"; do
+    if [ ! -e "${path}" ]; then
+        echo "ERROR: required path does not exist: ${path}" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+done
+
+mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}" "${WANDB_DIR}" "${HF_DATASETS_CACHE}"
+
+# Match the upstream launcher's behavior when OUTPUT_DIR already contains a
+# checkpoint. Trainer then restores optimizer, scheduler, and RNG state.
+LATEST_CKPT=$(ls -d "${OUTPUT_DIR}"/checkpoint-* 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n 1 || true)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Send a training-failure email using SMTP settings from the environment.
+
+Required environment variables:
+  SMTP_HOST, NOTIFY_EMAIL
+
+Optional variables:
+  SMTP_PORT       (default: 587)
+  SMTP_USER       (required by providers that require authentication)
+  SMTP_PASSWORD   (for Gmail, use an App Password rather than your login password)
+  SMTP_FROM       (default: SMTP_USER, otherwise NOTIFY_EMAIL)
+  SMTP_USE_SSL    (true for implicit TLS, normally false for port 587 STARTTLS)
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import smtplib
+import ssl
+import sys
+from email.message import EmailMessage
+
+
+def required(name: str) -> str:
+    value = os.environ.get(name)
+    if not value:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name} is required")
+    return value
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--subject", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--body", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        host = required("SMTP_HOST")
+        recipient = required("NOTIFY_EMAIL")
+        port = int(os.environ.get("SMTP_PORT", "587"))
+        username = os.environ.get("SMTP_USER")
+        password = os.environ.get("SMTP_PASSWORD")
+        sender = os.environ.get("SMTP_FROM") or username or recipient
+        use_ssl = os.environ.get("SMTP_USE_SSL", "false").lower() in {
+            "1", "true", "yes", "on"
+        }
+    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+        print(f"Email notification not sent: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    message = EmailMessage()
+    message["From"] = sender
+    message["To"] = recipient
+    message["Subject"] = args.subject
+    message.set_content(args.body)
+
+    context = ssl.create_default_context()
+    if use_ssl:
+        with smtplib.SMTP_SSL(host, port, context=context, timeout=30) as server:
+            if username:
+                server.login(username, password or "")
+            server.send_message(message)
+    else:
+        with smtplib.SMTP(host, port, timeout=30) as server:
+            server.ehlo()
+            server.starttls(context=context)
+            server.ehlo()
+            if username:
+                server.login(username, password or "")
+            server.send_message(message)
+    return 0
+
+

+

+PROJECT_DIR=${PROJECT_DIR:-"$(dirname -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}")"}
+GRACE_ROOT=${GRACE_ROOT:-"$(dirname -- "${PROJECT_DIR}")"}
+
+PROFILE_RUN_NAME=${PROFILE_RUN_NAME:-Qwen3-VL-2B-GRACE-W4G128-PROFILE-10STEP}
+PROFILE_OUTPUT_DIR=${PROFILE_OUTPUT_DIR:-"${GRACE_ROOT}/models/${PROFILE_RUN_NAME}"}

+
+mkdir -p "${PROFILE_OUTPUT_DIR}/profiling"
+
+MONITOR_PID=""

+        --query-gpu=timestamp,index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,power.draw,clocks.sm,clocks.mem \

+    MONITOR_PID=$!
+fi
+
+cleanup() {

+RUN_NAME="${PROFILE_RUN_NAME}" \
+OUTPUT_DIR="${PROFILE_OUTPUT_DIR}" \

+"${SCRIPT_DIR}/finetune_qwen3vl_2b_grace_4gpu_memory_safe.sh"

+class AdaptiveHorizonSelector:

+
+    The selector never uses ground-truth actions. Inputs may be [H,D] or
+    [S,H,D]. Multiple samples enable a diffusion-disagreement signal.
+    """

+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        candidates: list[int],
+        continuous_groups: list[dict[str, Any]],

+        uncertainty_threshold: float,

+            raise ValueError("candidates must contain positive horizons")
+        self.candidates = sorted(set(int(k) for k in candidates))
+        self.continuous_groups = continuous_groups
+        self.discrete_indices = [int(i) for i in discrete_indices]
+        self.dimension_scale = np.asarray(dimension_scale, dtype=np.float64)
+        if np.any(self.dimension_scale <= 0):
+            raise ValueError("dimension_scale entries must be positive")

+        self.change_order = int(change_order)

+        self.uncertainty_threshold = max(float(uncertainty_threshold), 1e-12)
+        self.event_threshold = float(event_threshold)
+        self.event_guard_steps = max(int(event_guard_steps), 0)
+        self.risk_threshold = float(risk_threshold)
+        self.change_weight = float(change_weight)
+        self.uncertainty_weight = float(uncertainty_weight)
+        self.event_weight = float(event_weight)
+        self.fixed_horizon = None if fixed_horizon is None else int(fixed_horizon)
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(cls, config: dict[str, Any]) -> "AdaptiveHorizonSelector":
+        selector = config.get("selector", config)
+        return cls(
+            candidates=selector["candidates"],
+            continuous_groups=selector["continuous_groups"],
+            discrete_indices=selector.get("discrete_indices", []),
+            dimension_scale=selector["dimension_scale"],
+            change_order=selector.get("change_order", 1),
+            change_threshold=selector["change_threshold"],
+            uncertainty_threshold=selector.get("uncertainty_threshold", 1.0),
+            event_threshold=selector.get("event_threshold", 0.5),
+            event_guard_steps=selector.get("event_guard_steps", 1),
+            risk_threshold=selector.get("risk_threshold", 1.0),
+            change_weight=selector.get("change_weight", 1.0),
+            uncertainty_weight=selector.get("uncertainty_weight", 1.0),
+            event_weight=selector.get("event_weight", 2.0),
+            fixed_horizon=selector.get("fixed_horizon"),
+        )

+    def _validate_actions(self, actions: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        array = np.asarray(actions, dtype=np.float64)
+        if array.ndim == 2:
+            array = array[None, ...]
+        if array.ndim != 3:
+            raise ValueError(f"actions must be [H,D] or [S,H,D], got {array.shape}")
+        if array.shape[-1] != self.dimension_scale.size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"action dimension {array.shape[-1]} does not match dimension_scale "
+                f"length {self.dimension_scale.size}"
+            )
+        if not np.isfinite(array).all():
+            raise ValueError("actions contain NaN or infinity")
+        if array.shape[1] < self.candidates[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"action horizon {array.shape[1]} is shorter than minimum candidate "
+                f"{self.candidates[0]}"
+            )
+        return array
+
+    def signals(self, actions: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
+        samples = self._validate_actions(actions)
+        scaled = samples / self.dimension_scale[None, None, :]
+        mean_scaled = scaled.mean(axis=0)
+        horizon = samples.shape[1]
+
+        change = np.zeros(horizon, dtype=np.float64)
+        group_changes: list[np.ndarray] = []
+        for group in self.continuous_groups:
+            indices = np.asarray(group["indices"], dtype=np.int64)
+            if indices.size == 0:
+                continue
+            values = mean_scaled[:, indices]
+            diff = np.diff(values, n=self.change_order, axis=0)
+            signal = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(diff), axis=1))
+            aligned = np.zeros(horizon, dtype=np.float64)
+            aligned[self.change_order :] = signal
+            group_changes.append(aligned)
+        if group_changes:
+            change = np.max(np.stack(group_changes, axis=0), axis=0)
+
+        if samples.shape[0] > 1:
+            uncertainty = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.var(scaled, axis=0, ddof=1), axis=1))
+        else:
+            uncertainty = np.zeros(horizon, dtype=np.float64)
+
+        event = np.zeros(horizon, dtype=np.float64)
+        mean_actions = samples.mean(axis=0)
+        for index in self.discrete_indices:
+            transitions = np.flatnonzero(
+                np.abs(np.diff(mean_actions[:, index])) >= self.event_threshold
+            ) + 1
+            for transition in transitions:
+                lo = max(0, int(transition) - self.event_guard_steps)
+                hi = min(horizon, int(transition) + self.event_guard_steps + 1)
+                event[lo:hi] = 1.0
+
+        risk = (
+            self.change_weight * (change / self.change_threshold)
+            + self.uncertainty_weight * (uncertainty / self.uncertainty_threshold)
+            + self.event_weight * event
+        )
+        return {
+            "risk": risk,
+            "change": change,
+            "uncertainty": uncertainty,
+            "event": event,
+        }

+    def select(self, actions: np.ndarray) -> HorizonDecision:
+        samples = self._validate_actions(actions)
+        horizon = samples.shape[1]
+        candidates = [candidate for candidate in self.candidates if candidate <= horizon]
+        signals = self.signals(samples)

+                if float(np.max(risk[:candidate], initial=0.0)) <= self.risk_threshold

+            reason = "largest_prefix_below_risk_threshold" if passing else "minimum_safe_fallback"
+
+        risky = np.flatnonzero(risk > self.risk_threshold)

+        return HorizonDecision(
+            horizon=int(selected),
+            max_risk=float(np.max(risk[:selected], initial=0.0)),
+            first_risky_offset=first_risky,
+            reason=reason,
+            risk_by_offset=risk,
+            change_by_offset=signals["change"],
+            uncertainty_by_offset=signals["uncertainty"],
+            event_by_offset=signals["event"],
+        )

+def _analysis_actions(archive: PredictionArchive) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, str]:
+    if archive.pred_actions_normalized is not None and archive.gt_actions_normalized is not None:
+        return archive.pred_actions_normalized, archive.gt_actions_normalized, "normalized"
+    return archive.pred_actions, archive.gt_actions, "physical"

+def _group_specs(config: dict[str, Any], action_dim: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    groups = list(config["analysis"]["groups"])
+    used: set[int] = set()
+    for group in groups:
+        indices = [int(index) for index in group["indices"]]
+        if not indices or min(indices) < 0 or max(indices) >= action_dim:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid indices for group {group.get('name')}: {indices}")
+        overlap = used.intersection(indices)
+        if overlap:
+            raise ValueError(f"Action groups overlap at dimensions {sorted(overlap)}")
+        used.update(indices)
+    return groups
+

+def per_offset_rows(archive: PredictionArchive, config: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    pred, gt, space = _analysis_actions(archive)
+    _, seeds, horizon, action_dim = pred.shape
+    groups = _group_specs(config, action_dim)
+    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for offset in range(horizon):
+        valid = archive.valid_mask[:, offset]
+        if not np.any(valid):
+            continue
+        for group in groups:
+            indices = np.asarray(group["indices"], dtype=np.int64)
+            error = pred[valid, :, offset][:, :, indices] - gt[valid, offset][:, None, indices]
+            abs_error = np.abs(error)
+            sq_error = np.square(error)
+            if seeds > 1:
+                uncertainty = np.sqrt(
+                    np.mean(np.var(pred[valid, :, offset][:, :, indices], axis=1, ddof=1), axis=1)
+                )
+            else:
+                uncertainty = np.zeros(int(valid.sum()), dtype=np.float64)
+            rows.append(
+                {
+                    "offset": offset,
+                    "group": str(group["name"]),
+                    "space": space,
+                    "anchors": int(valid.sum()),
+                    "prediction_samples": int(valid.sum()) * seeds,
+                    "mae": float(abs_error.mean()),
+                    "rmse": float(np.sqrt(sq_error.mean())),
+                    "p95_abs_error": float(np.quantile(abs_error, 0.95)),
+                    "mean_seed_disagreement": float(uncertainty.mean()),
+                }
+            )
+    return rows

+def _oracle_horizon(
+    pred: np.ndarray,
+    gt: np.ndarray,
+    valid: np.ndarray,
+    candidates: Iterable[int],

+    step_error = np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(pred - gt[None, ...]), axis=(0, 2)))
+    minimum = min(candidates)
+    passing = []
+    for candidate in sorted(set(int(value) for value in candidates)):
+        if candidate > valid.size or not bool(np.all(valid[:candidate])):
+            continue
+        if float(np.max(step_error[:candidate], initial=0.0)) <= threshold:
+            passing.append(candidate)
+    return max(passing) if passing else minimum

+def merge(paths: list[str | Path], output: str | Path) -> Path:
+    if not paths:
+        raise ValueError("At least one shard archive is required")
+    archives = [PredictionArchive.load(path) for path in paths]
+    reference = archives[0]

+            raise ValueError(f"Shard shape mismatch: {archive.shape} vs {reference.shape}")
+        if not np.array_equal(archive.seeds, reference.seeds):
+            raise ValueError("Shard seed lists differ")
+        if (archive.pred_actions_normalized is None) != (
+            reference.pred_actions_normalized is None
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Only some shards contain normalized actions")
+
+    pred = np.concatenate([archive.pred_actions for archive in archives], axis=0)
+    gt = np.concatenate([archive.gt_actions for archive in archives], axis=0)
+    valid = np.concatenate([archive.valid_mask for archive in archives], axis=0)
+    tasks = np.concatenate([archive.tasks for archive in archives])
+    suites = np.concatenate([archive.suites for archive in archives])
+    episodes = np.concatenate([archive.episode_ids for archive in archives])
+    anchors = np.concatenate([archive.anchor_steps for archive in archives])
+    pred_norm = (
+        np.concatenate([archive.pred_actions_normalized for archive in archives], axis=0)
+        if reference.pred_actions_normalized is not None
+        else None
+    )
+    gt_norm = (
+        np.concatenate([archive.gt_actions_normalized for archive in archives], axis=0)
+        if reference.gt_actions_normalized is not None
+        else None
+    )
+
+    keys = np.asarray(
+        [f"{suite}\0{task}\0{episode}\0{anchor}" for suite, task, episode, anchor in zip(
+            suites, tasks, episodes, anchors

+        duplicate = keys[np.unique(keys, return_counts=True)[1].argmax()]
+        raise ValueError(f"Duplicate anchor across shards: {duplicate!r}")
+    order = np.argsort(keys)
+    merged = PredictionArchive(
+        pred_actions=pred[order],
+        gt_actions=gt[order],
+        valid_mask=valid[order],
+        tasks=tasks[order],

+import argparse
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import yaml
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run four disjoint FastWAM collector shards")
+    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--gpus", default="0,1,2,4", help="Physical GPU ids; GPU 3 is display-only here")
+    parser.add_argument("--max-anchors", type=int)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    config_path = Path(args.config).expanduser().resolve()
+    with config_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        config = yaml.safe_load(handle)
+    output = Path(config["collector"]["output_archive"])
+    if not output.is_absolute():
+        output = (config_path.parent / output).resolve()
+    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+    gpu_ids = [value.strip() for value in args.gpus.split(",") if value.strip()]
+    if not gpu_ids:
+        raise ValueError("No GPU ids supplied")
+    shard_paths = [output.with_name(f"{output.stem}.shard{i:02d}{output.suffix}") for i in range(len(gpu_ids))]
+    processes: list[tuple[int, subprocess.Popen]] = []
+    for shard, (gpu, shard_path) in enumerate(zip(gpu_ids, shard_paths)):
+        env = os.environ.copy()
+        env["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = gpu
+        cmd = [
+            sys.executable,
+            "-m",
+            "adaptive_horizon.collect_fastwam",
+            "--config",
+            str(config_path),
+            "--device",
+            "cuda:0",
+            "--shard-index",
+            str(shard),
+            "--shard-count",
+            str(len(gpu_ids)),
+            "--output",
+            str(shard_path),
+        ]
+        if args.max_anchors is not None:
+            cmd.extend(["--max-anchors", str(args.max_anchors)])
+        log_path = shard_path.with_suffix(".log")
+        log_handle = log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8")
+        process = subprocess.Popen(
+            cmd,
+            cwd=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]),
+            env=env,
+            stdout=log_handle,
+            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+            text=True,
+        )
+        process._adaptive_log_handle = log_handle  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+        processes.append((shard, process))
+        print(f"shard={shard} physical_gpu={gpu} pid={process.pid} log={log_path}")
+
+    failures = []
+    for shard, process in processes:
+        return_code = process.wait()
+        process._adaptive_log_handle.close()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+        if return_code != 0:
+            failures.append((shard, return_code))
+    if failures:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Collector shards failed: {failures}; inspect shard logs")
+
+    merge_cmd = [
+        sys.executable,
+        "-m",
+        "adaptive_horizon.merge_archives",
+        "--output",
+        str(output),
+        *[str(path) for path in shard_paths],
+    ]
+    subprocess.run(
+        merge_cmd,
+        cwd=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]),
+        check=True,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# Adaptive FastWAM Action Horizon
+
+This directory is an isolated experiment package for choosing how many actions
+to execute from a fixed 32-action FastWAM prediction. It does **not** modify
+anything under `FastWAM/`.
+
+The controlled variable is the executed prefix `K`, not the generated token
+length:
+
+```text
+observe -> always predict H=32 -> choose K <= 32 -> execute K -> replan
+```
+
+This separation avoids an additional sequence-length distribution shift. It
+also makes the claim precise: adaptive execution saves model calls per
environment step; it does not make one model call cheaper.
+
+## What is measured
+
+The FastWAM training action loss is a flow-matching velocity loss. It requires
+ground-truth action and injected noise, so it is not an inference-time
+confidence score. The collector therefore saves final sampled actions and the
+analysis reports:
+
+- per-future-offset and per-action-group MAE/RMSE;
+- diffusion disagreement when multiple seeds are collected;
+- action-command curvature and gripper-event risk;
+- a predicted-only heuristic `adaptive_k`;
+- an offline `oracle_action_error_k` used only as a diagnostic upper bound.
+
+`oracle_action_error_k` is not a simulator-safe horizon. Closed-loop success is
+the final criterion.
+
+## Dataset semantics
+
+| Dataset | Action | Fixed prediction | Existing execution baseline |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| LIBERO | 3 translation deltas + 3 rotation deltas + gripper | 32 | 10 |
+| RoboTwin Aloha-AgileX | left 6 qpos + gripper + right 6 qpos + gripper | 32 | 24 |
+
+LIBERO's temporal `a[t+1]-a[t]` is a change in an already-delta command.
+RoboTwin's first qpos difference is joint displacement; its second difference
+is command curvature. The YAMLs encode this difference with `change_order`.
+
+## Environment
+
+```bash
+cd /raid/lvchengtao/fengshuyi/adaptive_action_horizon
+source /home/air/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+conda activate /raid/lvchengtao/envs/fastwam
+export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:${PYTHONPATH:-}"
+```
+
+## 1. Verify the analysis without a model
+
+Synthetic data is only a logic smoke test and is labelled as such:
+
+```bash
+python -m adaptive_horizon.make_synthetic \
+  --output runs/synthetic/predictions.npz
+python -m adaptive_horizon.analyze \
+  --config configs/synthetic_libero.yaml
+```
+
+Outputs are written to `runs/synthetic/analysis/`:
+
+- `per_offset.csv`
+- `per_task.csv`
+- `decisions.csv`
+- `per_offset.png`
+- `summary.json`
+
+## 2. Collect real FastWAM predictions
+
+Small LIBERO smoke run:
+
+```bash
+python -m adaptive_horizon.collect_fastwam \
+  --config configs/libero.yaml \
+  --device cuda:0 \
+  --max-anchors 1
+```
+
+The checked-in collector config selects two full-horizon anchors per task. Set
+`max_anchors_per_task: 0` for every eligible anchor. It deliberately rejects
+missing paths before allocating the model.
+
+For four A100s on this host (physical ids `0,1,2,4`; id `3` is the display
+GPU), run disjoint anchor shards and merge them automatically:
+
+```bash
+python scripts/run_collect_4gpu.py \
+  --config configs/libero.yaml \
+  --gpus 0,1,2,4
+```
+
+Then analyse:
+
+```bash
+python -m adaptive_horizon.analyze --config configs/libero.yaml
+```
+
+The RoboTwin config is aligned with FastWAM's 50-task Aloha-AgileX setup. Its
+release checkpoint and normalization stats exist locally, but the full
+RoboTwin LeRobot directory is not currently present. Update only
+`fastwam.dataset_dirs` in `configs/robotwin.yaml` when it is mounted, then use
+the same collector/analysis commands.
+
+## 3. Experimental protocol
+
+1. Keep model, checkpoint, seed set, scheduler and prediction horizon fixed.
+2. Split by episode/task; never let a window cross an episode boundary.
+3. Exclude padded offsets. Bootstrap confidence intervals by episode, not by
+   overlapping clips.
+4. Calibrate selector thresholds on training tasks/episodes only.
+5. Evaluate fixed `K` candidates, task-static best `K`, matched-random `K`,
+   adaptive `K`, and simulator oracle `K` on paired initial states.
+6. Report success rate, replans, mean executed `K`, model calls, model time,
+   wall time, collision/drop failures and gripper-event failures.
+7. Claim a win only if adaptive `K` improves the success/compute Pareto curve.
+
+Theoretical compute savings from an earlier optimization and fewer replans may
+multiply for the model-compute component. End-to-end speedup must still be
+measured because simulator and preprocessing time do not scale with `K`.
+
+## Tests
+
+```bash
+python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
+```
+
+## File map
+
+- `adaptive_horizon/collect_fastwam.py`: patch-free FastWAM dataset/model runner
+- `adaptive_horizon/archive.py`: safe NPZ interchange schema
+- `adaptive_horizon/metrics.py`: offset/group/task diagnostics
+- `adaptive_horizon/selector.py`: GT-free prefix selector
+- `adaptive_horizon/analyze.py`: CSV/JSON/plot report generator
+- `scripts/run_collect_4gpu.py`: four-GPU sharding and merge
+- `configs/libero.yaml`, `configs/robotwin.yaml`: all experiment knobs

+    archive: PredictionArchive,

+    """Summarise results by privileged/estimated target distance when supplied.

+    emitted only for archives augmented by a simulator or perception pipeline.

+    if distance.ndim == 2:

+        if offset < 0 or offset >= distance.shape[1]:
+            raise ValueError(f"analysis.distance_offset out of range: {offset}")
+        distance = distance[:, offset]
+    edges = np.asarray(

+        dtype=np.float64,

+        raise ValueError("analysis.distance_bins must be strictly increasing bin edges")
+    if distance.min(initial=0.0) < edges[0] or distance.max(initial=0.0) > edges[-1]:
+        raise ValueError("distance_to_target values fall outside analysis.distance_bins")
+    assignments = np.digitize(distance, edges[1:-1], right=False)
+    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

+        indices = np.flatnonzero(assignments == bin_index)
+        if not indices.size:

+        upper = edges[bin_index + 1]
+        label = (

+            if np.isinf(upper)

+# Experimental protocol
+
+## Claim being tested
+
+FastWAM always predicts `H=32`. The intervention changes only the executed
+prefix `K`: longer in low-risk free-space motion and shorter around alignment,
+grasp/contact and other high-risk events. This is a hypothesis. Action
+smoothness is not itself evidence of distance to an object.
+
+## Signals and their allowed use
+
+| Signal | Ground truth needed? | Online selector? | Interpretation |
+|---|---:|---:|---|
+| Final sampled action error by offset/group | yes | no | Offline prediction quality |
+| Training flow-matching velocity MSE | yes, plus sampled noise/timestep | no | Training objective/diagnostic only |
+| Temporal action activity | no | yes | Command change/curvature, not distance |
+| Diffusion sample disagreement | no | yes, but costs extra samples | Epistemic-style proxy, not calibrated risk |
+| Gripper transition | no | yes | Discrete event guard |
+| EEF-to-target distance | simulator state or perception | yes | Direct distance signal if definition is valid |
+| Closed-loop success/collision/overshoot | simulator | evaluation only | Final safety/task criterion |
+
+LIBERO dimensions `0:3` are delta translation, `3:6` delta rotation and `6`
+gripper. Therefore first temporal difference measures variation of an already
+delta command. RoboTwin's released FastWAM configuration uses 14-D dual-arm
+qpos: six joints plus gripper per arm. Its second temporal difference is the
+appropriate curvature/activity diagnostic.
+
+## Offline split
+
+1. Build deterministic anchors without crossing episode boundaries.
+2. Keep full prediction length at 32 and store final sampled actions, GT,
+   padding mask, task, episode, anchor and diffusion seed.
+3. Tune thresholds only on a calibration split; freeze them before task/seed
+   test evaluation.
+4. Report error and action activity per future offset and dimension group,
+   then per task. If target distance is available, report the same metrics in
+   preregistered distance bins.
+5. The action-error oracle is only an offline upper-bound proxy. Never call it
+   a safe horizon.
+
+For a 180-frame window with stride 10 there are 18 anchors (`0..170`), not 20.
+Requiring a full 32-step GT suffix leaves 15 anchors (`0..140`). Use padding
+masks if retaining the late anchors, and do not compare offsets with different
+effective sample counts without reporting those counts.
+
+## Closed-loop comparisons
+
+Use identical checkpoint, initial states, task instructions, inference seeds,
+schedule and 32-action prediction length. Compare:
+
+- fixed `K` grid: LIBERO `{1,2,4,8,10,16,24,32}`; RoboTwin
+  `{1,2,4,8,12,16,24,32}`;
+- original fixed baseline (`10` LIBERO, `24` RoboTwin);
+- task-static `K` selected without current observations;
+- random `K` matched to the adaptive method's marginal K distribution;
+- action-only adaptive selector;
+- distance-only selector when a valid distance signal exists;
+- combined selector;
+- privileged simulator oracle as an analysis ceiling, not a deployable method.
+
+Primary metric is success rate with paired episode seeds and bootstrap
+confidence intervals. Also report collisions, dropped objects, overshoot,
+episode control steps, replans/model calls, model time, simulator time and
+end-to-end wall time. Tune on clean settings and test both clean and randomized
+settings. Report every one of RoboTwin's 50 tasks rather than only an aggregate.
+
+## Speed accounting
+
+If an episode executes `T` controls, model calls are approximately
+`T / E[K]`. Increasing mean K from 10 to 20 can at most halve replanning calls;
+it does not halve the cost of one 32-action inference. A previous 4x method and
+this method may multiply only for the model-compute component if the mechanisms
+are independent. Measure end-to-end time before claiming 8x.
+

+# Adaptive FastWAM action horizon
+
+This directory is an isolated experiment package. It does not modify
+`../FastWAM`. The model always predicts 32 actions; the proposed policy selects
+and executes a prefix `K` before replanning.
+
+The central correction is important: FastWAM's `action_loss` is a masked
+flow-matching velocity MSE used during training. It needs the ground-truth
+action and sampled noise/timestep, so it is not available as an inference-time
+confidence score. This package uses final sampled action-vs-GT error only for
+offline analysis, and uses prediction-only action activity, sample disagreement
+and gripper events for the deployable selector.
+
+See [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md) for the hypothesis, 180-frame arithmetic,
+ablation matrix, action semantics and speed accounting.
+
+## What is included
+
+- `collect_fastwam.py`: deterministic task-stratified LIBERO/RoboTwin anchors,
+  fixed-32 inference, final predictions plus GT/padding metadata.
+- `analyze.py`: per-offset/per-group error, temporal Δ/curvature, diffusion
+  disagreement, per-task decisions, optional distance/phase stratification.
+- `selector.py`: chooses the largest candidate prefix below a calibrated risk
+  threshold without reading GT.
+- `run_collect_4gpu.py`: disjoint shards on physical GPUs `0,1,2,4`, then a
+  checked merge. GPU 3 in this machine is display-only.
+- `integrations/`: patch-free closed-loop wrappers for LIBERO and RoboTwin.
+- YAML files contain all paths, thresholds, dimensions and horizon candidates.
+
+## Environment and smoke test
+
+```bash
+cd /raid/lvchengtao/fengshuyi/adaptive_action_horizon
+source /home/air/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+conda activate /raid/lvchengtao/envs/fastwam
+python -m adaptive_horizon.make_synthetic --output runs/synthetic/predictions.npz
+python -m adaptive_horizon.analyze --config configs/synthetic_libero.yaml
+pytest -q
+```
+
+Synthetic output is a logic test only, not evidence for the research claim.
+
+## LIBERO offline collection
+
+One-anchor preflight:
+
+```bash
+python -m adaptive_horizon.collect_fastwam \
+  --config configs/libero.yaml --device cuda:0 --max-anchors 1 \
+  --output runs/libero/smoke.npz
+```
+
+Four disjoint GPU shards (start only when those GPUs have sufficient free
+memory):
+
+```bash
+python scripts/run_collect_4gpu.py --config configs/libero.yaml --gpus 0,1,2,4
+python -m adaptive_horizon.analyze --config configs/libero.yaml
+```
+
+The checked-in `max_anchors_per_task: 2` is a pilot. Increase it only after the
+preflight and use multiple episodes per task for the final study.
+
+## RoboTwin status
+
+The YAML exactly follows FastWAM's released setup: 14-D qpos action, three
+cameras, dual-arm Aloha-AgileX-style environment, fixed prediction horizon 32,
+baseline execution horizon 24 and 50-task coverage. The released checkpoint
+and normalization stats are present. The full LeRobot dataset expected at
+`data/robotwin2.0/robotwin2.0` is not mounted in this workspace, and this
+RoboTwin vendor checkout also lacks the normal task-config assets. Collection
+or closed-loop evaluation therefore fails preflight until those assets are
+provided; the code does not silently substitute a different dataset.
+
+## Outputs
+
+Analysis writes `per_offset.csv`, `decisions.csv`, `per_task.csv`, optional
+`per_distance_bin.csv` and `per_phase.csv`, a plot, and `summary.json`.
+`adaptive_k` is deployable; `oracle_action_error_k` uses GT and is offline only.

+def load_callable(spec: str | None) -> Callable[..., float] | None:
+    if spec is None or str(spec).strip().lower() in {"", "none", "null"}:
+        return None
+    module_name, separator, attribute = str(spec).partition(":")
+    if not separator:

+    """Undo LIBERO eval's gripper convention, then apply training normalizer."""
+    physical = np.asarray(action, dtype=np.float32).copy()

+    action_meta = processor.shape_meta["action"]
+    if len(action_meta) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Adaptive LIBERO wrapper expects one merged action field")
+    normalizer = processor.normalizer.normalizers["action"][action_meta[0]["key"]]
+    return normalizer.forward(torch.from_numpy(physical)).numpy()

+def _average_ranks(values: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+    order = np.argsort(values, kind="mergesort")
+    sorted_values = values[order]
+    ranks = np.empty(values.size, dtype=np.float64)
+    start = 0
+    while start < values.size:
+        end = start + 1
+        while end < values.size and sorted_values[end] == sorted_values[start]:
+            end += 1
+        ranks[order[start:end]] = 0.5 * (start + end - 1)
+        start = end
+    return ranks

+def _spearman(rows: list[dict[str, Any]], x_name: str, y_name: str) -> float | None:
+    if len(rows) < 3:

+    x = np.asarray([float(row[x_name]) for row in rows], dtype=np.float64)
+    y = np.asarray([float(row[y_name]) for row in rows], dtype=np.float64)

+## Original first-frame vs IDM action stage
+
+The scalar action-loss formula is the same: timestep-weighted, padding-masked
+flow-velocity MSE. The conditioning path is not the same. Original `FastWAM`
+encodes only the current image and denoises 32 action tokens from that image,
+language and proprio. `FastWAMIDM` first predicts a future video, freezes its
+full video tokens, then denoises actions conditioned on that predicted future;
+during training its action branch sees a teacher-forcing video branch.
+Optional-IDM trains a single checkpoint with a per-sample mask that alternates
+full-video and first-frame conditioning. Calling `first_frame` on that checkpoint
+uses the original inference routine, but not the original trained weights or
+training distribution, so it is not an interchangeable baseline and is not used
+in this package.

+# Original first-frame LIBERO pilot
+
+Date: 2026-09-03
+
+## Scope and provenance
+
+- Architecture: original `FastWAM` (`fastwam.runtime.create_fastwam`), not IDM
+  or Optional-IDM.
+- Checkpoint: `FastWAM/checkpoints/fastwam_release/libero_uncond_2cam224.pt`.
+- Dataset: four LIBERO v3 suites, 40 tasks, 1,712 episodes, 277,713 frames,
+  20 Hz, seven action dimensions.
+- Sample: 80 anchors, two per task. One is at episode progress 0; the second is
+  the latest stride-10 anchor retaining 32 actions plus the final observation.
+- Inference: fixed 32-action horizon, one diffusion seed (42), ten inference
+  steps. Analysis uses normalized final sampled actions against normalized GT.
+- Reproducible evidence: `runs/libero/predictions.npz` and
+  `runs/libero/analysis/`.
+
+## Findings
+
+| Slice | Anchors | Mean adaptive K | Fixed-10 prefix RMSE | Mean error-oracle K |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Episode start (`progress < .25`) | 40 | 31.6 | 0.0425 | 31.8 |
+| Later (`.50 <= progress < .75`) | 21 | 20.76 | 0.0288 | 30.10 |
+| Later (`.75 <= progress <= 1`) | 19 | 20.21 | 0.0328 | 30.32 |
+| Overall | 80 | 26.05 | — | 31.0 |
+
+Selected-K distribution: `{2: 1, 10: 5, 16: 16, 24: 10, 32: 48}`.
+The action-change signal has Spearman correlation `0.420` with max future-step
+action RMSE, while the configured combined risk has correlation only `0.037`.
+Late-episode shortening is dominated by gripper-transition guards: late anchors
+have mean event coverage `0.112`, versus `0.0055` at episode start.
+
+The action-error oracle is highly cutoff-dependent. With normalized max-step
+RMSE cutoffs `{.05, .10, .20, .50}`, its mean K is respectively
+`{14.38, 30.18, 31.0, 31.0}`; the adaptive policy exceeds that oracle in
+`{60%, 5%, 1.25%, 1.25%}` of anchors. No cutoff has yet been mapped to simulator
+failure, so none is a safety threshold.
+
+## Validation assessment: needs closed-loop validation
+
+The pilot supports a narrow statement: predictions contain signals that differ
+between early and late task stages, so a variable execution horizon is worth
+testing. It does **not** prove the distance hypothesis or the safety of the
+current selector.
+
+Material limitations:
+
+1. LIBERO records do not provide task-correct EEF-to-target distance; episode
+   progress and action Δ are proxies, not distance.
+2. Two anchors per task and one diffusion seed are a pipeline pilot, not a
+   statistically adequate final sample.
+3. First/last anchors come from different episodes, so episode seed and phase
+   are partially confounded.
+4. Offline imitation error is not closed-loop success, collision, overshoot or
+   dropped-object risk.
+5. Multi-seed uncertainty is unavailable with one seed; using several samples
+   online would directly reduce the intended speed benefit.
+
+The next decision gate is paired-seed closed-loop evaluation against fixed K,
+task-static K and matched-random K, with thresholds frozen before the held-out
+episodes. Object-distance claims require task-specific simulator state or a
+validated perception estimator.
+

+        cursor += calls
+        selected = np.asarray(
+            [int(row["selected_k"]) for row in episode_decisions], dtype=np.float64
+        )
+        infer_seconds = np.asarray(
+            [float(row["inference_seconds"]) for row in episode_decisions],
+            dtype=np.float64,
+        )
+        rows.append(
+            {
+                "policy": policy,
+                "episode": episode,
+                "success": int(episode in success),
+                "steps": int(steps),
+                "replans": calls,
+                "mean_selected_k": float(selected.mean()),
+                "min_selected_k": int(selected.min()),
+                "max_selected_k": int(selected.max()),
+                "planned_action_count": int(selected.sum()),
+                "model_inference_seconds": float(infer_seconds.sum()),
+                "mean_inference_seconds_per_call": float(infer_seconds.mean()),
+            }
+        )
+    return rows
+
+
+def _bootstrap_interval(values: np.ndarray, *, seed: int = 0) -> list[float]:
+    if values.size == 0:
+        return [float("nan"), float("nan")]
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    sampled = rng.choice(values, size=(10000, values.size), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
+    return [float(value) for value in np.quantile(sampled, [0.025, 0.975])]
+
+
+def summarize(
+    adaptive_result_path: str | Path,
+    adaptive_log_path: str | Path,
+    fixed_result_path: str | Path,
+    fixed_log_path: str | Path,
+    output_dir: str | Path,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    paths = [Path(path).expanduser().resolve() for path in (
+        adaptive_result_path, adaptive_log_path, fixed_result_path, fixed_log_path
+    )]
+    adaptive_result = json.loads(paths[0].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    fixed_result = json.loads(paths[2].read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if (
+        adaptive_result["task_suite"],
+        adaptive_result["task_id"],
+        adaptive_result["total_episodes"],
+    ) != (
+        fixed_result["task_suite"],
+        fixed_result["task_id"],
+        fixed_result["total_episodes"],
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Adaptive/fixed result populations are not paired")
+    adaptive = _episode_rows("adaptive", adaptive_result, _load_jsonl(paths[1]))
+    fixed = _episode_rows("fixed10", fixed_result, _load_jsonl(paths[3]))
+    episode_rows = adaptive + fixed
+
+    output = Path(output_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with (output / "episodes.csv").open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=list(episode_rows[0]))
+        writer.writeheader()
+        writer.writerows(episode_rows)
+
+    summary: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "task_suite": adaptive_result["task_suite"],
+        "task_id": adaptive_result["task_id"],
+        "episodes": adaptive_result["total_episodes"],
+        "policies": {},
+        "paired_differences_adaptive_minus_fixed10": {},
+        "warning": "A small integration run is not a safety or speed claim.",
+    }
+    for policy, rows, result in (
+        ("adaptive", adaptive, adaptive_result),
+        ("fixed10", fixed, fixed_result),
+    ):
+        summary["policies"][policy] = {
+            "success_rate": float(np.mean([row["success"] for row in rows])),
+            "mean_steps": float(np.mean([row["steps"] for row in rows])),
+            "mean_replans": float(np.mean([row["replans"] for row in rows])),
+            "mean_selected_k": float(np.mean([row["mean_selected_k"] for row in rows])),
+            "total_model_inference_seconds": float(
+                np.sum([row["model_inference_seconds"] for row in rows])
+            ),
+            "mean_inference_seconds_per_call": float(
+                np.mean([row["mean_inference_seconds_per_call"] for row in rows])
+            ),
+            "task_duration_seconds": float(result["duration"]),
+        }
+    for metric in ("success", "steps", "replans", "model_inference_seconds"):
+        differences = np.asarray(
+            [a[metric] - f[metric] for a, f in zip(adaptive, fixed)], dtype=np.float64
+        )
+        summary["paired_differences_adaptive_minus_fixed10"][metric] = {

+        json.dumps(summary, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+    return summary
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Summarize paired adaptive/fixed LIBERO runs")
+    parser.add_argument("--adaptive-result", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--adaptive-log", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--fixed-result", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--fixed-log", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    print(

+                args.fixed_result,
+                args.fixed_log,
+                args.output_dir,
+            ),

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import shutil
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+WORKSPACE = ROOT.parent
+DEFAULT_FASTWAM_VENDOR = WORKSPACE / "FastWAM" / "third_party" / "RoboTwin"
+DEFAULT_ROBOTWIN = ROOT / "third_party" / "RoboTwin"
+
+# These are the only common source files that differ between FastWAM's vendor
+# snapshot and upstream bf44be51. Refuse unexpected input instead of silently
+# copying a different local tree.
+EXPECTED_SHA256 = {
+    "envs/_base_task.py": "a4fa65537d2ba34206b89980b031e0bdc543561e01b0b1a0ae735617d577d2e7",
+    "script/eval_policy.py": "b214f2478744020dd49af026cf9fc14fcb0441bd0ace34005cd6774bfa367e3d",
+}
+
+
+def _sha256(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def sync(source_root: Path, target_root: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
+    copied: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+    for relative, expected_hash in EXPECTED_SHA256.items():
+        source = source_root / relative
+        target = target_root / relative
+        actual_hash = _sha256(source)
+        if actual_hash != expected_hash:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"FastWAM vendor file changed unexpectedly: {source}\n"
+                f"expected {expected_hash}, got {actual_hash}"
+            )
+        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        shutil.copy2(source, target)
+        copied.append(
+            {"path": relative, "sha256": actual_hash, "source": str(source.resolve())}
+        )
+
+    result: dict[str, object] = {
+        "source_root": str(source_root.resolve()),
+        "target_root": str(target_root.resolve()),
+        "files": copied,
+    }
+    manifest = target_root / "FASTWAM_OVERLAY.json"
+    manifest.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    return result
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Copy FastWAM's two RoboTwin compatibility patches into the isolated clone"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--source", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_FASTWAM_VENDOR)
+    parser.add_argument("--target", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_ROBOTWIN)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    print(json.dumps(sync(args.source, args.target), indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+

+def _replace_once(path: Path, old: str, new: str) -> str:
+    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    if new in text and old not in text:
+        return "already_patched"
+    count = text.count(old)
+    if count != 1:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Expected exactly one match in {path}, found {count}")
+    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")
+    return "patched"
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Apply the two patches required by FastWAM's pinned RoboTwin installer"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--prefix", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    site = args.prefix.expanduser().resolve() / "lib" / "python3.10" / "site-packages"
+    planner = site / "mplib" / "planner.py"
+    urdf_loader = site / "sapien" / "wrapper" / "urdf_loader.py"
+    changes = {
+        str(planner): _replace_once(
+            planner,
+            "if np.linalg.norm(delta_twist) < 1e-4 or collide or not within_joint_limit:",
+            "if np.linalg.norm(delta_twist) < 1e-4 or not within_joint_limit:",

+def _download_one(name: str, asset_dir: Path) -> str:

+def _verify(asset_dir: Path) -> None:
+    failures = []
+    for name, expected in FILES.items():
+        path = asset_dir / name
+        actual = path.stat().st_size if path.exists() else None
+        if actual != expected:
+            failures.append({"file": name, "expected_size": expected, "actual_size": actual})
+    if failures:
+        raise RuntimeError("Asset archive verification failed:\n" + json.dumps(failures, indent=2))
+
+
+def _safe_extract(archive_path: Path, asset_dir: Path) -> None:
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
+        root = asset_dir.resolve()
+        for member in archive.infolist():
+            destination = (asset_dir / member.filename).resolve()
+            if destination != root and root not in destination.parents:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Unsafe ZIP member in {archive_path}: {member.filename}")
+        archive.extractall(asset_dir)
+
+

+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Fetch pinned RoboTwin simulator assets into the isolated clone"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--robotwin-root", type=Path, default=ROBOTWIN)
+    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=3)
+    parser.add_argument("--extract-only", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    robotwin = args.robotwin_root.expanduser().resolve()
+    asset_dir = robotwin / "assets"

+    if not args.extract_only:

+            futures = {pool.submit(_download_one, name, asset_dir): name for name in FILES}
+            for future in as_completed(futures):

+"""Task-aware simulator distance for LIBERO ablation only.
+
+This reads privileged BDDL goal and MuJoCo state. It is not a deployable visual
+distance estimator and must be reported as an oracle ablation.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+
+
+def _domain(task_env: Any) -> Any:
+    current = task_env
+    for _ in range(4):
+        if hasattr(current, "parsed_problem") and hasattr(current, "object_states_dict"):
+            return current
+        current = getattr(current, "env", None)
+        if current is None:
+            break
+    raise TypeError("Could not unwrap LIBERO BDDL domain from task_env")
+
+
+def _position(domain: Any, object_name: str) -> np.ndarray:
+    if object_name not in domain.object_states_dict:
+        raise KeyError(f"Goal object/site {object_name!r} has no LIBERO state interface")
+    state = domain.object_states_dict[object_name].get_geom_state()
+    position = np.asarray(state["pos"], dtype=np.float64)
+    if position.shape != (3,) or not np.isfinite(position).all():
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid position for {object_name!r}: {position}")
+    return position
+
+
+def _is_grasped(domain: Any, object_name: str) -> bool:
+    if object_name not in domain.objects_dict:
+        return False
+    return bool(
+        domain._check_grasp(
+            gripper=domain.robots[0].gripper,
+            object_geoms=domain.get_object(object_name),
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def extract_distance(
+    *,
+    task_env: Any,
+    obs: dict[str, Any],
+    task_description: str,
+    cfg: Any,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return EEF distance to the next interaction target and audit metadata."""
+    del task_description, cfg
+    if task_env is None:
+        raise ValueError("Privileged LIBERO distance requires the current task environment")
+    domain = _domain(task_env)
+    goals = list(domain.parsed_problem.get("goal_state", []))
+    unfinished = [goal for goal in goals if not bool(domain._eval_predicate(goal))]
+    if not unfinished:
+        return {
+            "distance": 0.0,
+            "phase": "goal_complete",
+            "predicate": None,
+            "interaction_target": None,
+        }
+
+    goal = unfinished[0]
+    if len(goal) not in (2, 3):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported LIBERO goal predicate: {goal}")
+    predicate = str(goal[0])
+    source = str(goal[1])
+    grasped = _is_grasped(domain, source)
+    if len(goal) == 3 and grasped:
+        interaction_target = str(goal[2])
+        phase = "transport_to_goal"
+    else:
+        interaction_target = source
+        phase = "reach_or_interact"
+
+    eef = np.asarray(obs["robot0_eef_pos"], dtype=np.float64)
+    if eef.shape != (3,) or not np.isfinite(eef).all():
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid robot0_eef_pos: {eef}")
+    target = _position(domain, interaction_target)
+    return {
+        "distance": float(np.linalg.norm(eef - target)),
+        "phase": phase,
+        "predicate": predicate,
+        "source_object": source,
+        "interaction_target": interaction_target,
+        "source_grasped": grasped,
+        "unfinished_goal_count": len(unfinished),
+    }

+# Adaptive FastWAM action horizon
+
+This is an isolated LIBERO experiment package. It does not modify
+`../FastWAM`. All formal runs use the released original
+`libero_uncond_2cam224` checkpoint, its first-frame action architecture and
+`sigma_shift=5.0`. IDM and Optional-IDM are excluded.
+
+FastWAM still predicts 32 actions on every model call. The intervention is only
+the number `K` of actions executed before replanning. Therefore the possible
+gain is fewer model calls, not cheaper individual calls.
+
+## Current conclusion
+
+The training `action_loss` is correct for optimization but cannot select `K` at
+inference: it is a flow-velocity MSE requiring ground-truth actions, sampled
+noise and a timestep. Final sampled action-vs-GT error is allowed only as an
+offline diagnostic.
+
+The deployable single-sample proxy is temporal change in the predicted action.
+On the formal 800-anchor LIBERO archive its Spearman correlation with maximum
+future-step action RMSE is `0.293`, so it is useful enough to test but too weak
+to call a confidence score or a distance estimate. LIBERO dimensions `0:3` are
+delta translation, `3:6` delta rotation and `6` is gripper; differencing them
+measures command variation, not EEF-to-object distance.
+
+The selector now executes through the first predicted gripper transition and
+replans shortly after it. Stopping before the event caused receding-horizon
+starvation: the transition could remain just outside the executed prefix
+forever. A direct-distance variant exists only as a privileged simulator-state
+ablation and is not presented as deployable perception.
+
+See [PROTOCOL.md](PROTOCOL.md) for the preregistered comparisons and
+[PILOT_RESULTS.md](PILOT_RESULTS.md) for current evidence.
+
+## Reproduce the offline result
+
+```bash
+cd /raid/lvchengtao/fengshuyi/adaptive_action_horizon
+source /home/air/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+conda activate /raid/lvchengtao/envs/fastwam
+
+python -m adaptive_horizon.collect_fastwam \
+  --config configs/libero_offline_calibration.yaml --device cuda:0
+python -m adaptive_horizon.analyze \
+  --config configs/libero_offline_calibration.yaml
+python -m adaptive_horizon.compare_selector_configs \
+  --archive runs/libero/offline_calibration/predictions.npz \
+  --configs configs/libero_adaptive_ct04.yaml,configs/libero_adaptive_ct05.yaml,configs/libero_adaptive_ct06.yaml \
+  --output runs/libero/offline_calibration/selector_comparison
+pytest -q
+```
+
+For collection on this machine, `scripts/run_collect_4gpu.py` creates disjoint
+shards on physical GPUs `0,1,2,4` and checks the merge. GPU 3 is display-only.
+The launcher requires 28 GB free per selected A100.
+
+## Closed-loop calibration and held-out test
+
+Threshold candidates are chosen only on task ID 0 of each of the four standard
+LIBERO suites, paired with fixed `K=10` on identical initial states and seed:
+
+```bash
+python -u scripts/run_libero_closed_loop.py \

+This is an isolated LIBERO experiment package. It does not modify

+The training `action_loss` is correct for optimization but cannot select `K` at
+inference: it is a flow-velocity MSE requiring ground-truth actions, sampled
+noise and a timestep. Final sampled action-vs-GT error is allowed only as an
+offline diagnostic.

+The deployable single-sample proxy is temporal change in the predicted action.

+    the remainder of the process. Under ZeRO-3, parameters are gathered and
+    the rank-0 modification is redistributed on context exit.

+    if output_chunk_size <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("output_chunk_size must be positive")
+
+    def _merge(module: QATLoraLinear) -> None:
+        for start in range(0, module.out_features, output_chunk_size):
+            end = min(start + output_chunk_size, module.out_features)
+            delta = torch.matmul(module.lora_B[start:end], module.lora_A)
+            delta = delta.mul(module.lora_scaling).to(module.weight.dtype)
+            module.weight.data[start:end].add_(delta)
+        module.lora_A.zero_()
+        module.lora_B.zero_()
+

+    if is_zero3:
+        import deepspeed
+        try:
+            rank = torch.distributed.get_rank()
+        except Exception:
+            rank = 0
+        for _, module in model.named_modules():
+            if not isinstance(module, QATLoraLinear):
+                continue
+            params = [module.weight, module.lora_A, module.lora_B]
+            with deepspeed.zero.GatheredParameters(params, modifier_rank=0):
+                if rank == 0:

+            count += 1
+    else:
+        for _, module in model.named_modules():
+            if not isinstance(module, QATLoraLinear):
+                continue
+            _merge(module)
+            count += 1

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Compare full GRACE with QAT-LoRA GRACE and find the largest viable
+# micro-batch on physical GPUs 0,1,2. GPU 3 is never made CUDA-visible.
+#
+# Defaults run:
+#   full GRACE: batch 1, accumulation 12
+#   QAT-LoRA:   batch 1/2/3/4, accumulation 12/6/4/3
+#
+# Every case therefore processes 12 samples per GPU per optimizer step
+# (36 globally), making tokens/sec comparable despite different micro-batches.
+# The first profiled optimizer step is excluded from the steady-state summary.
+# Final model export is disabled: this is a speed/memory test, not training.
+#
+# Examples:
+#   BATCH_SIZES="1 2 3" ./scripts/profile_qwen3vl_2b_grace_lora_3gpu.sh
+#   RUN_BASELINE=0 PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS=5 \
+#       ./scripts/profile_qwen3vl_2b_grace_lora_3gpu.sh
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
+PROJECT_DIR=${PROJECT_DIR:-"$(dirname -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}")"}
+GRACE_ROOT=${GRACE_ROOT:-"$(dirname -- "${PROJECT_DIR}")"}
+
+# This default intentionally excludes physical GPU 3.
+PROFILE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${PROFILE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES:-0,1,2}
+NPROC_PER_NODE=3
+RUN_BASELINE=${RUN_BASELINE:-1}
+BATCH_SIZES=${BATCH_SIZES:-"1 2 3 4"}
+PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS=${PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS:-3}
+SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP=${SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP:-12}
+MODEL_MAX_LENGTH=${MODEL_MAX_LENGTH:-2048}
+MAX_PIXELS=${MAX_PIXELS:-50176}
+MIN_PIXELS=${MIN_PIXELS:-784}
+
+PROFILE_TAG=${PROFILE_TAG:-"$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"}
+PROFILE_ROOT=${PROFILE_ROOT:-"${GRACE_ROOT}/models/profiling/grace-lora-3gpu-${PROFILE_TAG}"}
+BASELINE_LAUNCHER="${SCRIPT_DIR}/finetune_qwen3vl_2b_grace_4gpu_memory_safe.sh"
+LORA_LAUNCHER="${SCRIPT_DIR}/finetune_qwen3vl_2b_grace_lora_4gpu_memory_safe.sh"
+
+case "${PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS}" in
+    *[!0-9]*|'') echo "ERROR: PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS must be an integer." >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac
+if [ "${PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS}" -lt 2 ]; then
+    echo "ERROR: use at least 2 optimizer steps so one warmup step can be excluded." >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+case "${SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP}" in
+    *[!0-9]*|'') echo "ERROR: SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP must be an integer." >&2; exit 1 ;;
+esac
+if [ "${SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP}" -le 0 ]; then
+    echo "ERROR: SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP must be positive." >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+for launcher in "${BASELINE_LAUNCHER}" "${LORA_LAUNCHER}"; do
+    [ -x "${launcher}" ] || {
+        echo "ERROR: launcher is missing or not executable: ${launcher}" >&2
+        exit 1
+    }
+done
+
+mkdir -p "${PROFILE_ROOT}"
+export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="${PROFILE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES}"
+export WANDB_MODE=disabled
+
+ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID=""
+stop_monitor() {
+    if [ -n "${ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID}" ]; then
+        kill "${ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        wait "${ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID=""
+    fi
+}
+trap stop_monitor EXIT INT TERM
+
+start_monitor() {
+    local output_file=$1
+    stop_monitor
+    if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null 2>&1 && nvidia-smi -L >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        nvidia-smi \
+            --id="${PROFILE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES}" \
+            --query-gpu=timestamp,index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total,power.draw,clocks.sm,clocks.mem \

+            --loop=1 >"${output_file}" 2>&1 &
+        ACTIVE_MONITOR_PID=$!
+    fi
+}
+
+run_case() {
+    local case_name=$1
+    local launcher=$2
+    local micro_batch=$3
+    local grad_accum=$4
+    local output_dir="${PROFILE_ROOT}/${case_name}"
+    local log_file="${output_dir}/launcher.log"
+    local status_file="${output_dir}/status.txt"
+
+    mkdir -p "${output_dir}/profiling"

+        echo "case=${case_name}"
+        echo "physical_gpus=${PROFILE_CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES}"
+        echo "nproc_per_node=${NPROC_PER_NODE}"
+        echo "micro_batch=${micro_batch}"
+        echo "gradient_accumulation=${grad_accum}"
+        echo "global_samples_per_optimizer_step=$((NPROC_PER_NODE * micro_batch * grad_accum))"

+    start_monitor "${output_dir}/profiling/nvidia_smi.csv"

+    MAX_STEPS="${PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS}" \
+    PROFILE_STEPS="${PROFILE_OPTIMIZER_STEPS}" \
+    PROFILE_DEEPSPEED_COMMS=False \
+    SKIP_FINAL_EXPORT=True \
+    PER_DEVICE_BATCH="${micro_batch}" \

+    MODEL_MAX_LENGTH="${MODEL_MAX_LENGTH}" \
+    MAX_PIXELS="${MAX_PIXELS}" \
+    MIN_PIXELS="${MIN_PIXELS}" \
+    SAVE_STEPS=1000 \

+    set -e
+    stop_monitor
+

+    else
+        echo "FAIL exit_code=${rc}" | tee "${status_file}"
+    fi
+    return "${rc}"
+}
+
+echo "Profiling directory: ${PROFILE_ROOT}"
+echo "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES} (physical GPUs 0,1,2 only)"
+
+if [ "${RUN_BASELINE}" = "1" ]; then
+    if ! run_case "full_grace_mb1" "${BASELINE_LAUNCHER}" 1 "${SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP}"; then
+        echo "WARNING: full-GRACE baseline failed; continuing with LoRA sweep." >&2
+    fi
+fi
+
+LORA_SUCCEEDED=0
+for micro_batch in ${BATCH_SIZES}; do
+    case "${micro_batch}" in
+        *[!0-9]*|'') echo "ERROR: invalid batch size: ${micro_batch}" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+    esac
+    if [ "${micro_batch}" -le 0 ]; then
+        echo "ERROR: batch sizes must be positive: ${micro_batch}" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+    if [ $((SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP % micro_batch)) -ne 0 ]; then
+        echo "ERROR: SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP=${SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP} is not divisible by batch ${micro_batch}." >&2
+        echo "Choose a common multiple of every requested batch size." >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+    grad_accum=$((SAMPLES_PER_GPU_STEP / micro_batch))

+class GraceLearningDiagnostics:
+    """Opt-in proof that adapters, QAT scales, and GRACE terms participate.
+
+    Parameter hooks capture backward signal before DeepSpeed can partition or
+    clear gradients. Small CPU snapshots then verify that trainable parameter
+    values actually change while a representative frozen QAT scale does not.
+    This is intentionally diagnostic-only because the extra norm reductions
+    perturb timing.
+    """

+    CATEGORIES = ("lora_A", "lora_B", "qat_scale", "merger", "other")
+
+    def __init__(self, enabled: bool, max_steps: int, output_dir: str):

+        self.max_steps = max(0, int(max_steps))
+        self.output_dir = output_dir
+        self.rank = _rank()
+        self.hook_handles = []
+        self.grad_sq = {}
+        self.grad_tensors = defaultdict(int)
+        self.term_stats = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(float))
+        self.snapshots = {}
+        self.records = []
+        self.pending = None
+        self.jsonl_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "learning_diagnostics.jsonl")
+        self.summary_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "learning_diagnostics_summary.json")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _category(name: str) -> str:
+        if name.endswith("lora_A"):
+            return "lora_A"
+        if name.endswith("lora_B"):
+            return "lora_B"
+        if name.endswith("log_scale"):
+            return "qat_scale"
+        if "merger" in name:
+            return "merger"
+        return "other"
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _numel(param) -> int:
+        return int(getattr(param, "ds_numel", param.numel()))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _sample(param, limit: int = 4096) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return param.detach().reshape(-1)[:limit].float().cpu().clone()
+
+    def install(self, student, teacher) -> None:
+        if not self.enabled:
+            return
+        if self.rank == 0:
+            os.makedirs(self.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
+
+        inventory = {
+            category: {"tensors": 0, "parameters": 0}
+            for category in self.CATEGORIES
+        }
+        frozen_scale = None
+        for name, param in student.named_parameters():
+            if param.requires_grad:

+                inventory[category]["tensors"] += 1
+                inventory[category]["parameters"] += self._numel(param)
+                if category not in self.snapshots:
+                    self.snapshots[category] = {
+                        "name": name,
+                        "param": param,
+                        "initial": self._sample(param),
+                    }
+
+                def capture(grad, category=category):
+                    if grad is not None:
+                        value = grad.detach().float().square().sum()
+                        self.grad_sq[category] = self.grad_sq.get(category, 0.0) + value
+                        self.grad_tensors[category] += 1
+                    return grad
+
+                self.hook_handles.append(param.register_hook(capture))
+            elif name.endswith("log_scale") and frozen_scale is None:
+                frozen_scale = {
+                    "name": name,
+                    "param": param,
+                    "initial": self._sample(param),
+                }
+
+        if frozen_scale is not None:

+    def observe_term(self, name: str, tensor: torch.Tensor, coefficient: float) -> None:

+"""Canonical RoboTwin rollout plans for paired closed-loop comparisons.
+
+RoboTwin first asks its motion-planning expert to screen simulator seeds, then
+chooses a language paraphrase with Python's global ``random`` module.  Both can
+vary across otherwise identical policy runs.  A paired comparison therefore
+needs to freeze both the accepted simulator seed and the exact instruction.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+
+_ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
+
+
+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as handle:
+        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
+            digest.update(block)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def _validate_episode_records(
+    records: Any,
+    *,
+    expected_episodes: int | None = None,
+) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    if not isinstance(records, list) or not records:
+        raise ValueError("rollout plan must contain a non-empty 'episodes' list")
+    normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for index, raw in enumerate(records, start=1):
+        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
+            raise ValueError(f"rollout plan episode {index} must be an object")
+        seed = raw.get("seed")
+        instruction = raw.get("instruction")
+        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
+            raise ValueError(f"rollout plan episode {index} has invalid seed {seed!r}")
+        if not isinstance(instruction, str) or not instruction.strip():
+            raise ValueError(f"rollout plan episode {index} has an empty instruction")
+        recorded_episode = int(raw.get("episode", index))
+        if recorded_episode != index:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"rollout plan episodes must be ordered 1..N; row {index} says "
+                f"episode={recorded_episode}"
+            )
+        normalized.append(
+            {"episode": index, "seed": int(seed), "instruction": instruction}
+        )
+    if expected_episodes is not None and len(normalized) != expected_episodes:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"rollout plan has {len(normalized)} episodes, expected {expected_episodes}"
+        )
+    seeds = [record["seed"] for record in normalized]
+    if len(set(seeds)) != len(seeds):
+        raise ValueError("rollout plan simulator seeds must be unique")
+    return normalized
+
+
+def load_rollout_plan(
+    path: Path,
+    *,
+    expected_episodes: int | None = None,
+    expected_task: str | None = None,
+    expected_task_config: str | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"rollout plan {path} must be a JSON object")
+    if expected_task is not None and payload.get("task_name") != expected_task:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"rollout plan task_name={payload.get('task_name')!r}, expected {expected_task!r}"
+        )
+    if (
+        expected_task_config is not None
+        and payload.get("task_config") != expected_task_config
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "rollout plan task_config="
+            f"{payload.get('task_config')!r}, expected {expected_task_config!r}"
+        )
+    payload["episodes"] = _validate_episode_records(
+        payload.get("episodes"), expected_episodes=expected_episodes
+    )
+    return payload
+
+
+def read_episode_log(
+    path: Path,
+    *,
+    expected_episodes: int | None = None,
+) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    rows = [
+        json.loads(line)
+        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+        if line.strip()
+    ]
+    if expected_episodes is not None and len(rows) != expected_episodes:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path} has {len(rows)} rows, expected {expected_episodes}")
+    for index, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
+        if int(row.get("episode", -1)) != index:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{path} episodes must be ordered 1..N; row {index} says "
+                f"episode={row.get('episode')!r}"
+            )
+    return rows
+
+
+def legacy_seeds_from_eval_log(
+    path: Path,
+    *,
+    expected_episodes: int | None = None,
+) -> list[int]:
+    clean = _ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
+    seeds = [int(value) for value in re.findall(r"current seed:\s*(\d+)", clean)]
+    if expected_episodes is not None and len(seeds) != expected_episodes:
+        raise ValueError(f"{path} has {len(seeds)} accepted seeds, expected {expected_episodes}")
+    if len(set(seeds)) != len(seeds):
+        raise ValueError(f"{path} contains duplicate accepted seeds")
+    return seeds
+
+
+def plan_from_episode_log(
+    episodes_path: Path,
+    *,
+    task_name: str,
+    task_config: str,
+    expected_episodes: int,
+    eval_log_path: Path | None = None,
+    source_run: str | None = None,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    rows = read_episode_log(episodes_path, expected_episodes=expected_episodes)
+    recorded_seeds = [row.get("eval_seed") for row in rows]
+    if all(isinstance(seed, int) and not isinstance(seed, bool) for seed in recorded_seeds):
+        seeds = [int(seed) for seed in recorded_seeds]
+        seed_source = "episodes.jsonl:eval_seed"
+    else:
+        if eval_log_path is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{episodes_path} lacks eval_seed; pass the matching legacy eval.log"
+            )
+        seeds = legacy_seeds_from_eval_log(
+            eval_log_path, expected_episodes=expected_episodes
+        )
+        seed_source = "legacy eval.log:current seed"
+    episodes = _validate_episode_records(
+        [
+            {
+                "episode": index,
+                "seed": seed,
+                "instruction": row.get("instruction"),
+            }
+            for index, (seed, row) in enumerate(zip(seeds, rows), start=1)
+        ],
+        expected_episodes=expected_episodes,
+    )
+    return {
+        "version": 1,
+        "task_name": task_name,
+        "task_config": task_config,
+        "episodes": episodes,
+        "source_run": source_run,
+        "seed_source": seed_source,
+    }
+
+
+def write_rollout_plan(path: Path, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(
+        json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Create a canonical RoboTwin seed+instruction rollout plan"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--episodes-jsonl", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--eval-log", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--task-name", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--task-config", default="demo_clean")
+    parser.add_argument("--episodes", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--source-run")
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    payload = plan_from_episode_log(
+        args.episodes_jsonl.resolve(),
+        task_name=args.task_name,
+        task_config=args.task_config,
+        expected_episodes=args.episodes,
+        eval_log_path=args.eval_log.resolve() if args.eval_log else None,
+        source_run=args.source_run,
+    )
+    write_rollout_plan(args.output.resolve(), payload)
+    print(
+        f"wrote {len(payload['episodes'])} paired rollouts to {args.output.resolve()}"
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# RoboTwin paired fixed-K curve expansion
+
+Frozen before the new closed-loop outcomes are inspected. Date: 2026-09-05.
+
+## Decision
+
+Screen 15 previously untested RoboTwin tasks under `demo_clean` to determine:
+
+1. which tasks are sensitive to execution horizon;
+2. whether offline `E(32)-E(10)` growth predicts `success@16-success@32`;
+3. how the frozen task-static `{16,24,32}` lookup compares with global fixed K.
+
+This is an exploratory screening run (`20` episodes per task/arm), not a
+confirmatory benchmark.
+
+## Arms and pairing
+
+- checkpoint: released `robotwin_uncond_3cam_384.pt`
+- `sigma_shift=5.0`
+- prediction horizon: `H=32`
+- executed fixed K: `{16,24,32}`
+- reference arm: `fixed24`
+- policy/diffusion seed: `0`
+
+For every task, `fixed24` runs first and freezes a canonical list of 20 records:
+the accepted simulator seed, exact unseen-language instruction, initial robot
+state hash, and initial three-camera-plus-state observation hash. The `fixed16`
+and `fixed32` arms must reproduce every canonical field exactly before their
+first action. A mismatch fails the job rather than silently changing the paired
+sample.
+
+The earlier five-task pilot did not freeze either accepted simulator seeds or
+language paraphrases. Its marginal success rates remain exploratory context,
+but it is not pooled into paired tests from this run.
+
+## Task selection
+
+The 15 tasks are fixed in `configs/robotwin_curve15_tasks.txt`. Selection rules:
+
+- exclude the five tasks in the existing closed-loop pilot;
+- include all five tasks named in the handoff as having the lowest offline
+  adaptive mean K (`stack_blocks_three`, `place_cans_plasticbox`, `grab_roller`,
+  `lift_pot`, `open_laptop`);
+- favor long tasks (12/15 have a step limit of at least 700);
+- retain coverage across the already frozen task-static strata: 4 tasks mapped
+  to K=16, 5 to K=24, and 6 to K=32.
+
+## Readout
+
+Report both quality and cost:
+
+- per-task and aggregate success rate;
+- model calls, executed steps, selected K, inference seconds, and wall time per
+  episode;
+- exact paired McNemar tests keyed by `(task, simulator_seed)`;
+- task-static lookup using each task's pre-existing K assignment;
+- Spearman correlation between offline error growth and task-level
+  `success@16-success@32`.
+
+For screening only, flag a task as visibly K-sensitive when the best and worst
+arms differ by at least 3/20 episodes (15 percentage points), and flag it as
+non-saturated when at least one arm is at or below 85%. These thresholds select
+follow-up tasks; they are not significance claims.
